clue.text: Serviceman flogged, one hears, on a regular basis

parts.note: to flog is British slang for to sell, so flogged gives sold
one is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: taking every other letter of the word hears, at regular intervals

explanation.surface: A serviceman is whipped, rumour has it, again and again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one hears' looks like a sound signal, but 'on a regular basis' takes the alternate letters E and R from 'hears'.
explanation.definitionFit: A soldier is a member of the armed services, a serviceman in the army.

clue.text: Is tense leaving communist party

indicators.note: these letters leave the longer word

parts.note: a communist is broadly a socialist
taken as written
T is the grammar abbreviation for tense

explanation.surface: A tense member quits the Communist party.
explanation.definitionFit: A social is an informal party or gathering.

clue.text: Begin meal gobbling starter in anger

indicators.note: the meal gobbles, or swallows, the letter

parts.note: lunch is a meal

indicators.note: the starter is the first letter of anger

explanation.surface: Someone starts eating, wolfing a first course in a rage.
explanation.definitionFit: To launch something is to start or set it going.

clue.text: Sob implies travelling is out of the question

indicators.note: the letters travel to new positions

explanation.surface: A tearful insinuation that a journey cannot happen.
explanation.definitionFit: Something out of the question cannot happen at all.

clue.text: In dire trouble, like in the past

indicators.note: the letters lie in the run of the words dire trouble

explanation.surface: Someone was badly in trouble, as in earlier times.
explanation.definitionFit: A retro style imitates fashions from earlier decades.

clue.text: Relating to a low point in the main?

definitions.text: Relating to a low point in the main?

parts.words: Relating to a low point in the main?
parts.note: the main is a poetic word for the ocean, and its lowest point lies far beneath the surface

explanation.surface: It sounds like a query about the weakest part of something principal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the main' is an old literary name for the open ocean, so a low point in it is somewhere far down below the waves.
explanation.definitionFit: Describing the ocean's depths, such as fishing or diving far from the surface, uses this compound adjective.

clue.text: Rash itching

definitions.meaning: reckless, done without regard to danger
eager, longing badly to do something

explanation.surface: A rash that is itchy.
explanation.definitionFit: A desperate act is reckless; being desperate to go means badly wanting to.

clue.text: Reportedly exercise farm animals

indicators.note: signals that the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: to exercise a right is to use it

explanation.surface: Supposedly someone takes the farm animals out for exercise.
explanation.definitionFit: Female sheep are livestock kept on farms.

clue.text: What arachnophobe might do when encountering a spider? Make haste!

definitions.text: What arachnophobe might do when encountering a spider?
definitions.meaning: someone afraid of spiders might tread on one

explanation.surface: A spider-phobic person is told to be quick about it.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for hurrying, originally pressing the accelerator, matches the literal act of treading on the spider.

clue.text: Shivering on stairs, one starts a fire

indicators.note: shivering shakes the letters into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone shivering on the stairs lights a fire to warm up.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who deliberately sets fires is a fire-raiser.

clue.text: Penny is after china mug

indicators.note: the penny letter comes after the friend in the answer

parts.note: china means mate in Cockney rhyming slang (china plate = mate), hence a chum

explanation.surface: A penny comes after a china mug, as in a shop's price tag.
explanation.walkthrough: 'china' is Cockney rhyming slang: china plate = mate, so a friend.
explanation.definitionFit: A mug in British slang is a gullible fool, which a chump also is.

clue.text: Experience the French ship with no relish?

parts.note: to experience something can be to taste it
le is the French masculine word for the
SS stands for steamship

explanation.surface: Someone tries out the French ship and finds the food bland.
explanation.definitionFit: Food lacking any relish or flavour is bland and insipid.

clue.text: Usual cat charged around person? On the contrary

indicators.note: one piece is placed around the other
says the containment runs the other way round, so the charged word goes around the cat word

parts.note: someone charged with a crime is accused
a tom is a male cat

explanation.surface: An ordinary cat is charged and sits around a person, or perhaps the reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: Taken literally the surface puts the cat around someone charged; 'On the contrary' tells the solver to swap container and contents, so 'person' only describes who is charged.
explanation.definitionFit: Something one is used to is habitual, the usual thing, as in an accustomed seat.

clue.text: Certainly not working when it's lunchtime?

parts.note: a firm refusal is no
a machine that is working is on

explanation.surface: Someone refuses to work at lunchtime.
explanation.definitionFit: Midday, twelve o'clock, is the traditional hour for a midday meal.

clue.text: Criminal isn't idly crossing court, clearly

indicators.note: the scrambled letters cross over, enclosing, the court letters
criminal suggests something bent or wrong, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A criminal doesn't loiter while crossing the courtyard, plainly.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying something plainly and unmistakably is saying it clearly.

clue.text: Uniform features of missile with air moving across it

indicators.note: the scrambled letters stretch across the word it, which sits inside them
the letters of missile and air are set moving into a new order

explanation.surface: A missile flies through the air, with the air moving across it.
explanation.definitionFit: Points of likeness are resemblances; uniform here means alike.

clue.text: Critical time to support one chap swallowing alcohol

indicators.note: in a down clue the time letter sits beneath and so supports the rest

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: the man swallows, or contains, the drink

parts.note: a chap is a man
port is a fortified wine

explanation.surface: A crucial moment for helping a fellow who drinks.
explanation.definitionFit: Something critical is of great consequence, vitally significant.

clue.text: Approaches adult very entertained by balls

parts.note: A is the film-rating abbreviation for adult

indicators.note: the very letter is entertained, held as a guest, inside the dances

parts.note: balls are formal dances

explanation.surface: A grown-up is amused by the balls and makes approaches.
explanation.definitionFit: Advances are approaches, especially romantic overtures toward someone.

clue.text: Calm relative with good prayers

parts.note: an even temper is a calm one
a son is a relative

explanation.surface: A placid relation, being good, says their prayers.
explanation.definitionFit: The Anglican evening service consists of prayers and canticles.

clue.text: Send me vet and lop off growths

indicators.note: off means gone bad or awry, so these letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: An instruction to call the vet and cut something off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lop off' reads as a phrase, but 'off' is the anagram signal on SEND ME VET and LOP.
explanation.definitionFit: Growths in the sense of advances or progress are developments.

clue.text: Pinch the Spanish coin

parts.note: to pinch is to nick, to steal
el is Spanish for the

explanation.surface: Steal the Spaniard's coin.
explanation.definitionFit: The US five-cent piece is called by the metal it was made from.

clue.text: Become old, caught in New York office

parts.note: to age is to grow old

indicators.note: the caught letter goes in the New York letters

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: Someone grows old trapped in a New York office.
explanation.definitionFit: A business bureau, such as a travel or employment firm, is an office.

clue.text: On the way back, teen carefully squeezes spots

indicators.note: On the way back says the hidden letters are read backwards
the phrase squeezes, or holds inside it, the letters wanted

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A teenager carefully squeezes their pimples.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'squeezes spots' as the definition, leaving the hidden word without an indicator; 'squeezes' is the containment signal, and 'spots' alone defines.
explanation.definitionFit: Acne is the skin condition marked by pimples, the spots teenagers suffer.

clue.text: Now in drag, ultimately acting as host

parts.note: the present is now, the current moment

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of drag

explanation.surface: A drag act currently performing as the compere.
explanation.definitionFit: A television host is said to be presenting a show.

clue.text: Take small bird

parts.note: the teal is a small duck

explanation.surface: Catch a small bird.
explanation.definitionFit: To take without permission is to pilfer or rob.

clue.text: Angry Greek god turned up

indicators.note: in a down clue, turned up means read from bottom to top

parts.note: Eros is the Greek god of love

explanation.surface: An irate Greek deity arrived.
explanation.definitionFit: Sore is an informal, chiefly American, word for annoyed or cross.

clue.text: After church eat cool, fresh food

indicators.note: the scrambled letters come after the church letters
fresh means new, so the letters of eat cool are made into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: After the church service, eat some cool fresh food.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweet made from cocoa is a foodstuff.

clue.text: Military volunteers man captured

parts.note: the TA, the Territorial Army, is Britain's volunteer reserve force
Ken is a man's name

explanation.surface: Volunteer soldiers take a man prisoner.
explanation.walkthrough: The TA (Territorial Army) was the name of Britain's part-time volunteer army reserve.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone seized as a prisoner has been captured.

clue.text: Son, for example, intended to cut out a piece

parts.note: S is the genealogical abbreviation for son

indicators.note: the letter A is removed from the word for intended

parts.note: what one intended is what one meant

explanation.surface: Someone meant to cut out a piece, using a son as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: A section or portion of something is a segment.

clue.text: Friend following leaders in London obstinately, yet in a faithful manner

indicators.note: the friend comes after the leading letters
the leaders are the opening letters of the three words London, obstinately and yet

parts.note: an ally is a friend

explanation.surface: A friend trails the bosses in London, stubborn yet faithful.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting with loyalty means doing so faithfully.
